name: section
description: One band of a page. Eleven of them on the marketing site, spelled eight different ways — `px-5 py-12 sm:px-8 sm:py-14`, then `py-14 sm:py-16`, then `py-16 sm:py-20` — which is a vertical rhythm decided eight times rather than once. The gutter and the rule travel with it, because a section that sets its own padding and forgets its own divider is how a page loses its rhythm one edit at a time.

inner.$description: The measure. A section is full-bleed and its CONTENT is not — separating the two is what lets a band carry a colour to the edges while the text still stops at a readable width.

band.$description: A full-bleed band in the brand tone, carrying the one text colour a band has. The page's turning point, used sparingly — two on the home page.

measure.$description: Narrower content for a section that is mostly prose.

a11y.note: A `<section>` is only a landmark when it has an accessible name, which is why `labelledBy` is on the interface rather than optional-by-habit. An unnamed section is a generic div to a screen reader, and a page of eleven of them gives a screen-reader user no way to skip between them.
